newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - US bond futures stage orderly pullback.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - US bond futures stage orderly pullback.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures were still on track to extend Friday's advance despite a lack of followthrough this week, technical analysts said Wednesday.

September bond futures have been floating backward since racing to finish at a three-month high of 111-09 on Friday. Strong volume and a rise in open interest accompanied the rally, suggesting further gains, according to conventional market wisdom. The gains never materialized.
"It has been a little bit of a fakeout for people so far," said Walter Burke, senior technical analyst at MCM Moneywatch.
But technicians were not throwing in the towel on the rally.
Burke said September bonds near term could still reach 112-16, a measured move objective from the April-to-May advance.
September futures were trading 4/32 higher at 110-21 Wednesday afternoon.

The market Tuesday staged an orderly pullback to 110-12, the halfway retracement of Friday's surge from 109-15 to 111-09, and has retested the level at the low this session, Burke said. More support lies at 110-09 to 110-08, the top of the May trading range, he said.
"As long as we hold that breakout level, this could just be a normal return to the breakout level," he said.

He noted that hourly momentum indicators had shifted from overbought after Friday's runup to approaching oversold and should emit a buy signal next, while the potential also exists for a bullish divergence on a quick push below 110-12.

James Bianco of Arbor Trading said a strong recent correlation of bond price gains with jumps in open interest suggested rallies such as Friday's were getting fuel from "panic buying" as latecomers jumped on the bandwagon.
Open interest in bond futures rose a hefty 27,000 contracts Friday, then shed almost all of that gain in two subsequent sessions, CBOT figures show.
Daily open interest increases and rising bond prices have an 87 percent correlation rate over the past 50 days, Bianco said.
If that pattern persists, he said he would expect the speculative buying interest in bond futures eventually to dry up, paving the way for futures to revisit 108-00 in the next three or four weeks.

Futures still could muster the strength to push beyond 112-00 before turning down again, Bianco said, adding he would interpret any divergence from the open interest pattern on an upward price day as a bullish sign because it would imply the futures had found stronger hands. -- Susan Kelly, Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
